newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees drop in wheat imports after tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees drop in wheat imports after tax rise.

text.p: Turkish officials said on Monday they expected wheat imports by private companies to fall after a weekend decree curbing wheat and corn imports by raising taxes.
"We do not think private companies, especially millers, would go for wheat imports this year any more," said one senior farm official.
"This is because we have enough wheat and the quality is good," he told Reuters at an international grains conference in southern Turkey.
The official reiterated earlier official estimates that Turkey would have a bumper wheat harvest of about 19 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 15.5 million tonnes last year.
But Western trade reports put Turkey's wheat output at about 16.5 million tonnes this year.
Turkey's Islamist-led coalition government on Saturday raised taxes on non-seed wheat and corn imports to 15 percent from three in a move to promote use of the domestic crop and protect farmers.
Import barriers were lowered two years ago to encourage imports to make up for what were then disappointing crops.
But pasta producers said they would still go for imports of durum wheat, despite the new import tax worth some $30 per tonne, saying the domestic durum quality was not satisfactory.

Official figures, supplied by Tuncer Macinli of the foreign trade undersecretariat (DTM) on Monday, showed Turkey imported 1,253,331 tonnes of wheat in 1995, up sharply from 243,678 tonnes a year ago.
But unofficial estimates, according to wheat traders and millers, show at least 1.65 million tonnes were imported in 1995, including 500,000 tonnes by the Turkish Grain Board (TMO).
Officials said private millers and pasta producers had imported about 800,000 tonnes of wheat so far this year.

Macinli, deputy general manager of the DTM's export department, told the conference that Turkey's wheat imports in past years were mainly to meet seed needs as well as the durum needs of pasta producers.
Turkey's grain balance varies between deficit or slight surplus from year to year.
